UNH.rationale: UNH presents an extremely unattractive risk-reward profile. The franchise is high-quality (scale, vertical integration, defensive revenue), but the valuation has completely disconnected from fundamentals. Trailing P/E has tripled from ~10x to ~30x over 12 months while net margin halved (5.6% to 2.8%) and ROE collapsed from 22.8% to 12.3%. Earnings yield of 3.3% sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.68%, implying negative equity risk premium. The Q2 2026 beat ($6.38 vs $4.94 consensus) and guidance raise to $19.50-$20.00 are real positives, bringing forward P/E to ~21x — but this still demands sustained execution against structural commercial headwinds (medical cost trends >11%, No Surprises Act adding 100bps, margin recovery pushed past 2027). Berkshire Hathaway exited at a loss in Q1 2026. The stock has nearly doubled from its 52-week low of $234.60 to $421.47, and the re-rating far outpaces the fundamental improvement. With only one confirmed strong quarter (Q1 2026) and one beat (Q2 2026) after a severe margin trough in Q2/Q3 2025, the market is pricing a recovery that is not yet proven durable. The wide analyst target dispersion ($284-$492) confirms genuine uncertainty. At current levels, any earnings disappointment would trigger outsized multiple compression given the negative equity risk premium.
